description: XC-2/D-356 — the credentials spine, built against docs/SURFACES.md §'The credential law' (the existing spec — not re-derived): secrets never ride payloads or environments; credential.use@1 is a capability only the user-signed Recipe can grant (law 7) and NO in-sandbox composition grants it — the live path is dead by construction, fail-closed if provoked. Ops: credential.put@1 (MUTATION, consent-gated by policy rule — storing a credential is the security-sensitive bar; the sandbox stores sim-synthetic REFERENCE rows only, never material), credential.use@1 (READ, capability-gated by the recipe layer), credential.redact@1 (READ — M12's redaction-before-append surface: REDACTION_POLICY_V1 versioned policy data applied to captured bytes BEFORE the vault sees them; output-only, cannot reveal secrets).

contract.doc: put {credentialId, sim: true, meta?} → vault.append@1 (ns credentials, id credential:<credentialId>) → {credentialId, rev, record}. Stores a sim-synthetic REFERENCE row; refuses any payload carrying value/secret/key material (fail-closed) and any non-sim put (live secrets never enter the sandbox — SURFACES.md credential law 3). Consent required by policy rule (D-356).

use {credentialId} → {credential, rev} — the by-reference flow: the caller presents credentialId, the spine returns the reference row (sim-synthetic in-sandbox; a live owner-machine tier would exchange it for secret material per-call, post-v1). Capability-gated: only the user-signed Recipe grants port:credential.use@1; no in-sandbox composition grants it.

redact {bytes} → {redacted, redactions, policyVersion} — applies REDACTION_POLICY_V1 (versioned, inspectable policy data owned HERE — credential-derived patterns are the spine's domain, not regex spaghetti in a consumer) to captured text BEFORE it is appended to the vault (M12). Output-only: returns redacted bytes, never secret material.

capabilities.justification: Reference rows persist in the USER'S VAULT (ns 'credentials') via port:vault.append@1; use resolves a row via port:vault.get@1. The composition grants exactly these two per user-signed Recipe — never this manifest. Nothing here can read a secret: no secret material exists in the sandbox at all (SURFACES.md credential law 1–3).
